problems.title: Uniform Group Spanning Tree

source.preview_scope: group-level; not a complete variant specification

inference_basis_fields: contentPreview: K-1 edges, no cycle between groups
problems.inferred_spec: Inferred deterministic form of uniform sampling: there are (product of group sizes) * N^(K-2) ways to join K groups (N nodes) with K-1 cross-group edges into a tree (count 1 when K=1). rank (decimal string, 0 <= rank < count) selects one: peel mixed-radix digits e_i = rank mod |group i| for i = 0..K-1 (then divide), then p_j = rank mod N for j = 0..K-3 (then divide). Node list = groups concatenated in order; p_j names a node and its group forms a Pruefer sequence. Decoding: repeatedly take the smallest group not yet removed and no longer present in the rest of the sequence, emit [groups[leaf][e_leaf], node p_j], remove it; finally emit [groups[u][e_u], groups[v][e_v]] for the last two groups u < v. Drawing rank uniformly yields a uniform valid edge set.
problems.inference_uncertainty: very high: the preview only defines a valid edge set; the uniform-sampling aspect, the rank interface and the bijection are entirely inferred
problems.effects: arguments (including nested containers) unchanged; fresh returned containers
